text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
* Four prisoners have been convicted of murdering a fellow inmate in a cell at Windhoek Police station while in an alcohol and drug-crazed stupor.
* A former Koevoet fighter, John Deegan in a 50-page submission yesterday told the Truth and Reconciliation Commission in South Africa about atrocities committed against Swapo fighters.
* The President of the Namibian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (NNCCI), Joan Guriras, yesterday said the hostile behaviour of customs and immigration officials was scaring away investors.
* The European Commission is to support the democratisation process in Namibia with projects to the tune of N$1.6 million.
* The moratorium on the issuing of gambling licenses, issued in December will remain in place despite the completion of an investigation into gambling by the Damaseb-commission.
* Three of the six prisoners charged with the murder of a fellow inmate at the Windhoek Police cells have been sentenced to 22 years in prison, a fourth was given a 14-year sentence.
